title: The Boys' Home Thomas Barnardo Opened at 18 Stepney Causeway
conflicts: Opening date: December 1870 (DNB 1912), September 1870 (Higginbotham), 1867 (EB 1911, wrong); story says 1870. Arbitration: DNB (by Barnardo's co-memoirist James Marchant) says charges 'fully refuted', while Higginbotham reports criticism of his photographs and solitary confinement; story gives both. The boy turned away died 'two days' (Barnardo's) or 'a few nights' (Higginbotham) later; story says two days, attributed to the charity's history.
notes: The Jim Jarvis night is told as Barnardo's own account, flagged as told many times with varying details and with no other witness; I could not load a historian's direct critique of it. The staged photographs and the 1877 arbitration are in the last paragraph. The Guardian (2002) article on his altered images loads for the checker but WebFetch cannot read it, so it is not cited. Quote stance: complicates.
